allocations.item: Evening opening, 13 weeks (responsible person + utilities + cleaning)
Late bus subsidy: one minibus on the Northside–Kiln Field loop, 13 weeks
Additional Youth Studio sessions (partner can supply up to 4 extra sessions per month at the quoted price)
Staff training: welcome and access awareness, 2 days

chosen_pilot.name: Thursday Lates — transport-linked evening opening pilot
chosen_pilot.why: In the 2023 pilot, evening attendance was 38% higher than the same weeks the previous year and most new evening attendees came from Northside and Kiln Field; attendance fell back when the minibus stopped. The new doorstep survey confirms transport is the dominant barrier among residents who know the centre (57%), while 48% of estate households have never heard of it. This plan replicates the evening-plus-transport bundle for 13 weeks, caps every evening event at 60 to comply with the new accessible-entrance licensing condition, and adds a targeted mailer, the Youth Studio expansion (40-name waiting list; up to 4 extra sessions a month for the same £6,500), and welcome/access training. The lift is deferred to a separate £27,500 capital bid because lift + evening + bus would cost £51,500, £3,500 over the £48,000 envelope.
target_segments: existing and lapsed Evening Talks attendees
disabled visitors and people with access needs

changed_since_round_1.change: Removed the lift repair from the funded plan and deferred it to a separate £27,500 capital bid.
changed_since_round_1.why: The lift was re-quoted from £22,000 to £27,500 and its lead time rose from six to eight weeks. The round-1 three-line plan (lift + evening opening + minibus) would now cost £51,500, which is £3,500 over the £48,000 envelope. The lift cannot be phased (a part-share would not buy a usable repair), and capital cannot be swapped with revenue without a council variation, so the only compliant choice was to drop the lift or the transport link. The plan keeps the transport link because the 2023 pilot and the new estates survey identify transport as the dominant barrier among residents who know the centre.

changed_since_round_1.change: Capped every evening event at 60 attendees and kept the first floor closed.
changed_since_round_1.why: The new building-control condition requires the accessible entrance to be operable before any evening event with more than 60 attendees is licensed, whether or not it uses the first floor. With the lift deferred, the cap is the lawful way to run a ground-floor evening programme. The first floor has no costed programme and remains closed.

changed_since_round_1.change: Added the £4,200 targeted mailer to Northside and Kiln Field households.
changed_since_round_1.why: The new doorstep survey finds 48% of estate households have never heard of the centre, so awareness is a real barrier for about half. Among residents who have heard, 57% name getting home after an evening event as the main barrier. The mailer is a specific audience with a specific offer (weekly evening programme plus late minibus), which meets the board's 2022 test, and is not a repeat of the £9,000 borough-wide print campaign.

changed_since_round_1.change: Funded the Youth Studio expansion at £6,500, now described as up to four additional sessions a month rather than two.
changed_since_round_1.why: The partner's written clarification confirms supply fell, not interest: unique participants rose from 71 to 115 and there is a 40-name waiting list. The partner can supply staff for up to four extra sessions a month for the same £6,500. The interview speculation that young people had 'moved on' is withdrawn.

changed_since_round_1.change: Added the £2,800 welcome and access training.
changed_since_round_1.why: The 60-attendee cap, the accessible entrance still being out, and the need to record access needs all depend on front-of-house confidence. The training was deferred in round 1 for lack of budget room; deferring the lift freed room for it.

changed_since_round_1.change: Recomputed the budget to £37,500 committed across five quoted revenue lines, with £10,500 uncommitted.
changed_since_round_1.why: The five lines are the maximum defensible commitment under the current evidence. The lift (£27,500) cannot be phased and a part-share would not buy a usable repair, the print campaign (£9,000) is rejected on the 2022 evidence, and the café refresh (£7,500) is no longer available this quarter (U4). The £10,500 lapses, not carried.

changed_since_round_1.change: Removed the lift workstream from the pilot and replaced it with a week-1 ground-floor access gate and the 60-attendee cap.
changed_since_round_1.why: The pilot no longer waits for a lift handover. It can run only if the ground floor has an independent step-free route and accessible toilet; if it does not, the pilot does not start and the board must re-plan. The first floor stays closed all quarter.

changed_since_round_1.change: Replaced the lift-commissioning metric with an access-compliance and 60-cap metric, and added metrics for the youth expansion, the mailer, and the training.
changed_since_round_1.why: The lift is no longer a plan milestone, so reporting it as one would overstate what the plan delivers. The new metrics match the five funded lines and the current licensing condition. The attendance, estate-share, bus-use, end-time and equalities thresholds are unchanged.

The £37,500 revenue plan would fit inside a 15%-reduced £40,800 envelope if the quotes hold, with £3,300 headroom, whereas the round-1 £46,000 plan would not. The lift would still not fit and remains a separate capital decision.

changed_since_round_1.change: Removed the café equipment refresh from the option set.
changed_since_round_1.why: U4 defers it to the next financial year, so it is no longer available this quarter. The supplier change from Bean & Co to Harbour Roasters has no programming budget effect, and the refresh was already rejected as unrelated to programming.

changed_since_round_1.change: Rewrote all eight deliverables so the pilot, options, budget, metrics, plan, uncertainties and decisions describe the same £37,500 plan.
changed_since_round_1.why: The new material changes the budget and the access position, so leaving any round-1 figure in place would create inconsistency. The transport priority, the 92% survey caveat, the rejection of the borough-wide print campaign, the 2023 evidence, and the no-new-post rule are preserved because the new material does not change them.

evidence_assessment.claim: 92% (285/310) of respondents were satisfied or very satisfied; 89% would recommend the centre; 87% said the programme meets their needs.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The 310 forms were handed out in person at the free-entry Family Saturday weekend of 1–2 March 2025. The sample is self-selected, 71% travelled by car, and 78% attended with children under 12; it includes no non-visitors, weekday or evening audience, priority-estate quota, disabled-visitor breakdown, or equalities data. It cannot be generalised to the centre's audiences.

evidence_assessment.claim: The survey covers the people who come on a Saturday; non-visitors and weekday/evening audiences were not surveyed because the free-entry weekend was a family event.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The note confirms the coverage gap but provides no denominator, non-response analysis, or estate/equalities breakdown. It is an authors' caveat, not a representative sample design.

evidence_assessment.claim: A doorstep survey of 120 Northside and Kiln Field households found 48% have never heard of the centre, 37% have heard but never attended, and 15% have attended at least once. Among those who have heard, 57% name getting home after an evening event as the main barrier, 22% cost, and 11% 'nothing there interests me'.
evidence_assessment.limitation: A small doorstep survey, not a representative borough survey; the barrier percentages are based on the roughly half who have heard of the centre. It measures stated barriers, not behaviour, and the equalities team explicitly says it has not tested whether awareness alone converts to attendance. It is household-level, not programme-level, so it cannot answer which of the centre's programmes reach the estates.

evidence_assessment.claim: Sessions fell from 4 a month (January–May 2024) to 2 a month from June 2024. Monthly visits fell from 196–210 to 118–152, but visits per session rose from 49.0–52.5 to 59.0–76.0, and monthly unique participants rose from 71 to 115.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Monthly unique participants are not deduplicated across months. The data support a supply constraint, but they do not by themselves quantify unmet demand; the partner's waiting list is the better measure, and it is not a full demand curve.

evidence_assessment.claim: The partner youth organisation confirms its funding changed in June 2024 and it cut delivery from four sessions a month to two; that is the whole reason monthly visits fell. Unique participants rose from 71 (January 2024) to 115 (March 2025), and it now holds a waiting list of 40. It can supply staff for up to four extra sessions a month for the coming quarter at the same £6,500, using the waitlist first. The interview speculation that young people had 'moved on' is withdrawn.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The waiting list is not deduplicated or audited in the pack, and the offer of up to four extra sessions depends on the centre providing room and materials. The £6,500 is the same quoted price, not a new quote for a larger scope; the plan must confirm room capacity in week 1.

evidence_assessment.claim: The youth worker said numbers were down and speculated that young people had moved on, but also said sessions ran less often because of staffing and filled when they ran.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The speculative part of the interview has been withdrawn in writing by the partner organisation (U3). The interview is still useful as evidence of the staffing constraint, but it should not be cited for the 'lost interest' claim.

evidence_assessment.claim: Evening Talks ran twice a month, stopped in July–August 2024, returned in September 2024, and averaged 46.5 visits per session in 2025 Q1 (279 visits over 6 sessions) against 36.5 in April–June 2024 (219 visits over 6 sessions).
evidence_assessment.limitation: Small monthly numbers, no neighbourhood or equalities breakdown, and no explanation in the data for the 2024 gap. Monthly unique participants are not deduplicated. The recovery is consistent with demand, but it does not identify the cause.

evidence_assessment.claim: Evening attendance was 38% higher than the same weeks the previous year, the majority of new evening attendees came from Northside and Kiln Field, and attendance fell back to pre-pilot levels and new estate attendees stopped when the minibus funding ended.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Single site, 12 weeks, autumn, no contemporaneous control group, and no exact counts or estate denominators. The +38% may include novelty and seasonal effects, although the reversal after the bus stopped is strong evidence that transport was the binding constraint.

evidence_assessment.claim: A £9,000 borough-wide print and poster campaign produced attendance within normal seasonal variation, no measurable change in first-time attendance from the priority estates, and word of mouth remained dominant at 64%; the board minuted not to repeat the poster spend without a specific audience and a specific offer.
evidence_assessment.limitation: One 2022 campaign, with no specific offer or audience targeting. It does not prove all targeted communications are ineffective, but it directly rules out repeating the same broad scope. The new doorstep survey shows awareness is uneven, which supports a targeted mailer rather than a repeat of the broad campaign.

evidence_assessment.claim: Most regulars drive; the two estates are described as a bus change and a walk away; the last bus back is 19:10, so anything finishing after seven is no use to them.
evidence_assessment.limitation: One staff view, not a measured travel survey. It is consistent with the survey's 71% car figure, but the survey sample is Family Saturday attendees only. The interview says 'a bus change and a walk' while constraints.md says two bus changes; the plan uses the conservative two-change figure, and there is no estate-level travel data.

evidence_assessment.claim: The accessible entrance and passenger lift are out of service; any public event using the first floor is not permitted until the lift is returned to service; the repair is capital, now quoted at £27,500 with an eight-week lead, cannot be phased, and the accessible entrance must be operable before any evening event with more than 60 attendees is licensed, whether or not it uses the first floor.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The pack gives no contractor detail, building-condition survey, capital/revenue split, or costed first-floor programme. It also does not say whether the ground floor has an independent step-free route. The new condition is a licensing rule, not proof that the ground floor is independently accessible.

evidence_assessment.claim: The lift contractor re-quoted the repair at £27,500 (from £22,000) with an eight-week lead (from six weeks) because the parts are obsolete and must be remanufactured. The building control officer adds the condition that the accessible entrance must be operable before any evening event with more than 60 attendees is licensed.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The quote is still an estimate, not a fixed-price contract; contractor availability and building condition are unknown. The eight-week lead means public use from week 9 at the earliest if instructed in week 1. The £5,500 increase makes the round-1 three-line plan £51,500 and unaffordable within the £48,000 envelope.

evidence_assessment.claim: The café coffee supplier changes from Bean & Co to Harbour Roasters from next month. The café equipment refresh is deferred to the next financial year and is no longer available in this quarter's plan. Prices to visitors are unchanged.
evidence_assessment.limitation: This is an information notice with no programming budget effect. The refresh was already rejected as unrelated to programming in round 1; U4 makes it unavailable as well as irrelevant. The supplier change does not affect the plan's costs or participation rationale.

evidence_assessment.claim: The board has not answered whether 92% means audience development can stop, whether young people lost interest, why the 2023 pilot stopped working, what is safe to stop if the council cuts, and which programmes reach the priority estates.
evidence_assessment.limitation: These are questions, not evidence. The new doorstep survey helps with the awareness and barrier picture but does not answer the programme-level reach question; the plan's registration data is the beginning of an answer.

metrics.name: Evening attendance per session
metrics.baseline: 36.5 visits per session (Evening Talks, Apr–Jun 2024: 219 visits / 6 sessions); 2025 Q1 is 46.5
metrics.target: ≥50 visits per session by week 6, sustained to week 13 (about +37% on the 2024 baseline); hard cap 60, with cap hits and turn-aways reported

metrics.name: Priority-neighbourhood share of new evening attendees
metrics.baseline: Not measured by the centre; the 2023 pilot recorded a majority of new evening attendees from Northside and Kiln Field, without counts or denominators; the new doorstep survey gives a household baseline (15% attended at least once), not a programme baseline
metrics.target: ≥50% of new evening attendees from Northside or Kiln Field, with postcode/estate recorded

metrics.name: Late minibus use
metrics.baseline: 0 — no late service; last regular bus 19:10
metrics.target: ≥50% of priority-estate attendees use the 21:30 return; zero reported stranded attendees

metrics.name: Access compliance and 60-attendee cap
metrics.baseline: Accessible entrance and lift out of service; first-floor public events prohibited; no current evening programme; new condition requires the accessible entrance before any evening event >60 is licensed
metrics.target: 100% of evening events at or below 60; zero first-floor public events; ground-floor step-free route and accessible toilet confirmed in week 1. The lift is a separate £27,500 capital bid, not a plan milestone.

metrics.name: Equalities monitoring completeness
metrics.baseline: No neighbourhood or equalities breakdown in attendance.csv or the survey; the new doorstep survey is estate-level, not centre-attendance-level
metrics.target: ≥95% of pilot registrations record postcode/estate and access needs; council report covers both estates by week 13

metrics.name: Pilot attendee experience
metrics.baseline: 92% overall satisfaction (285/310), Family Saturday sample only; no estate or disability breakdown
metrics.target: ≥90% satisfied or very satisfied; results reported by estate, disability, and first-time status (n≥100)

metrics.name: Youth Studio expansion (funded)
metrics.baseline: 76 visits per session, 2 sessions/month, 115 monthly unique participants (Mar 2025); waiting list of 40
metrics.target: Up to 4 additional sessions/month (6 total), waitlist first; ≥70 visits per session; waitlist reduced or cleared; report actual delivery and any room/materials constraint

metrics.name: Targeted mailer reach and attribution
metrics.baseline: No mailer this quarter; no centre-level estate source data; doorstep survey household baseline: 48% never heard, 37% heard but never attended, 15% attended at least once
metrics.target: Mailer dispatched in weeks 1–2; every new estate registration attributed to a channel; report the mailer's incremental reach and cost per new estate attendee; do not repeat if it adds no measurable reach

metrics.name: Welcome and access training
metrics.baseline: No training this quarter recorded in the pack
metrics.target: 100% of front-of-house staff and volunteers trained before the first event; access actions logged and reviewed at week 6

uncertainties: The 92% satisfaction figure comes from a self-selected, in-person sample at a free-entry Family Saturday weekend (310 forms; 71% car; 78% with under-12s). It does not represent non-visitors, weekday/evening audiences, priority-estate residents, disabled visitors, or the wider borough.

The new doorstep survey is small (120 households) and measures stated barriers, not behaviour. The 57% transport finding is among the roughly half who have heard of the centre, so the base is small; the equalities team has not tested whether awareness alone converts to attendance.

There is still no centre-level neighbourhood attendance or equalities baseline, so the pack cannot say which programmes reach Northside and Kiln Field. The 50% estate-share target is a planning target, not a measured programme baseline.

The 2023 evening pilot was a single-site, 12-week autumn test with no contemporaneous control. The +38% figure may include novelty and seasonal effects, although the fall-back after the minibus stopped is strong evidence that transport was binding.

The Youth Studio waiting list of 40 is not audited or deduplicated in the pack, and the offer of up to four extra sessions a month depends on the centre providing room and materials. The £6,500 is the same quoted price, not a new quote for a larger scope.

The front-of-house interview describes the estates as 'a bus change and a walk' away, while constraints.md says two bus changes. The plan uses the conservative two-change figure, but the actual journey burden is not measured.

The lift is now £27,500 with an eight-week lead, and the round-1 three-line plan (lift + evening + bus) would cost £51,500, £3,500 over the £48,000 envelope. The lift cannot be phased (a part-share would not buy a usable repair), and capital cannot be swapped with revenue without a council variation, so it is deferred to a separate capital bid.

The new building-control condition requires the accessible entrance before any evening event with more than 60 attendees is licensed. The plan caps events at 60, but the cap may truncate demand; cap hits and turn-aways must be reported, and the cap cannot be raised without the accessible entrance and licensing confirmation.

It is not clear whether the ground floor has an independent step-free route and accessible toilet. If it does not, the pilot cannot run accessibly before the lift is commissioned; the plan makes this a week-1 verification gate and does not assume the 60 cap solves it.

The lift is a separate £27,500 capital bid and is not funded in this plan. The first floor remains closed, and no first-floor programme is costed. If the bid fails, the access position is unchanged for another quarter.

The evening rota has no named responsible person; the £9,600 assumes existing staff are extended, not a new post. Overtime, TOIL, cover, and 1.5 FTE capacity are not costed separately, and the pilot cannot start without a named person for all 13 evenings.

The minibus quote does not specify route stops, capacity, wheelchair accessibility, driver/safeguarding arrangements, or reliability. The 21:30 return assumes events end by 21:00, and bad weather or no-shows could strand attendees.

Demand from the estates at a weekly frequency is unproven. The 2023 pilot was talks/film, and the pack has no price sensitivity or content-preference data. The pilot may attract existing evening attendees rather than new estate residents, which is why estate share is a primary metric.

The targeted mailer is a test, not a proven fix. The household list, dispatch timing, and attribution are uncertain; if it adds no measurable new estate reach, it should not be repeated. A borough-wide print campaign is not the fallback.

The council's possible 15% next-quarter reduction is verbal and unconfirmed. The £37,500 revenue plan would fit inside a £40,800 envelope if the quotes hold, with £3,300 headroom, but the lift would not fit and remains a separate capital decision.

The plan leaves £10,500 uncommitted because no quoted line fits: the lift is £27,500 and cannot be phased; a part-share would not buy a usable repair; print is rejected, and the café refresh is no longer available. This is deliberate headroom, not a carry-over; the board may require a written variation to commit the full envelope.

The plan is all revenue (£37,500), so it needs the five lines to be revenue-eligible. If the £48,000 envelope is capital-only, the plan is not compatible and must be re-planned; the pack does not state the split.

Evaluation is a small, self-selected, single-site pilot with no control group. Results will be descriptive, and seasonal or novelty effects cannot be separated cleanly from the pilot's effect. The 60 cap and self-reported mailer attribution further limit what can be claimed.

The youth expansion, mailer, and training are funded, but the lift, borough print campaign, and café refresh are not. The lift is a genuine access need deferred to a separate capital bid; the print campaign is rejected on the 2022 evidence; the café refresh is unavailable this quarter.
